title: Text Adventure Game
story: Dark Cave — You awaken in a dim cavern. Exits: North, East. A rusty sword lies nearby. An old key glints in the corner. The door north is locked. Solve the puzzles, collect the items, find the treasure, escape. A complete multi-room text adventure.
why: The text adventure combines structs for rooms, Map for world, Vec for inventory, match for commands, enums for directions — a full game architecture in one file.
analogy: A Dungeons & Dragons dungeon map on graph paper: rooms are numbered circles, exits are lines connecting them, items are drawn inside the circles. Your text adventure is the computer reading the map aloud: 'You're in room 3. Sword on the floor. Exits: North, East.'
try_it: Add 5+ rooms with puzzles (locked doors, hidden passages, trap rooms). Add NPCs that give quests or trade items. Implement 'use [item]' to combine items or solve puzzles. Add a win condition: find the Golden Chalice in room 9.
tips: Store rooms in a Vec indexed by room ID — exits are (direction, room_id) pairs
Move player by changing current_room index — simple and fast
Check locks BEFORE moving — returns 'locked' message instead of changing room
common_mistakes: Allowing movement through locked doors — check requires_key before moving
Not updating room state when items are taken — item stays on floor forever
Using Strings for direction matching when enums would prevent typos
